about: The island's settlements, the anchor people the world tensions hang on, the roads people carry goods on, and the situations every side must agree on. author_world.py drafts the rest of each settlement's households and every sheet from this and bible.md (docs/SEEDED_LIVES.md).

settlements.name: Brackenford
settlements.brief: The walled market town. Farmers, the Market Guild's traders, gate guards, masons and carpenters short of stone, cooks and the innkeeper, chapel sisters who heal, scribes who keep the ledger. Proud of its square and its charter. Most of its people think Kettlebridge folk are grasping and cold, and the Coldwell outlaws thieves who had their chance.
settlements.ledger: Brackenford. The gates are kept by the town. The market is for anyone who comes in peace. Goods not grown in Brackenford's fields pay the gate-due: one mark a load, or a share. Thornby owes the town store forty baskets of grain.

anchors.name: Aldric Marrow
anchors.role: Reeve of Brackenford; keeps the gate-due and the town ledger; took the Coldwell fields for the town store in the Lean Year; old, and has not named who comes after him
ties: rival of Mercy Abbot over the gate-due
holds Thornby's debt against Osric Dunn
outlawed Marta Hale and her household
the broken match shamed him before Josiah Crane

anchors.name: Tobin Marrow
anchors.role: captain of the gate guards and the Reeve's son; broke his promise to marry Hester Crane two years ago and married Wenna
ties: commands Wat Fenner at the gate
thinks the outlaws must be cleared from the stone road

anchors.name: Wenna Marrow
anchors.role: Tobin's wife, a weaver's daughter who farms the Marrow strip; expecting their first child
ties: knows the town thinks she cost it the Kettlebridge peace

anchors.name: Mercy Abbot
anchors.role: head of the Market Guild; wants the gate-due dropped and trade with Kettlebridge back; holds the lease of the old Coldwell fields, which the Tolleys farm for the Guild
ties: trades with Silas Pike and wants more of his stone

anchors.name: Wat Fenner
anchors.role: gate guard at the south gate on the stone road; collects the gate-due from carters
ties: brother-in-law of Marta Hale, an outlaw
takes the due from Silas Pike

anchors.name: Agnes Fenner
anchors.role: cook at the inn; Marta Hale's younger sister; grew up at Coldwell
ties: SECRET: carries food out to Coldwell by the south gate when Wat is not on watch; Marta knows, Wat does not

anchors.name: Sister Elspeth
anchors.role: eldest sister of the chapel; keeps the common fire and the calendar; heals anyone who comes, outlaws included
ties: tended Marta Hale's son through a fever at Coldwell last winter

settlements.name: Kettlebridge
settlements.brief: The hill town of brick and iron. Masters and apprentices of the works and foundries, masons and quarriers, builders, a few farmers on the terraces, cooks, a clockkeeper-scribe, carters. Governed by the Works Council of masters. Proud, exact, short of food. Many think Brackenford folk are smug and lazy behind their walls. Lanternquay families from the Surge live on the poor terrace.
settlements.ledger: Kettlebridge Works Council. Apprentices are bound by indenture until their term. Stone is sold at the Council's price. Runaway apprentices are to be returned to their masters.

anchors.name: Josiah Crane
anchors.role: foundry master and chair of the Works Council; the broken match was an insult to his house; sends stone south to Lanternquay as much as north
ties: despises Aldric Marrow and his son Tobin
master of the runaway apprentice Pell, and wants him back

anchors.name: Hester Crane
anchors.role: keeps the foundry's books; once promised to Tobin Marrow
ties: corresponds with Mercy Abbot about reopening trade
SECRET: was relieved when Tobin broke the match; she did not want to leave the works

anchors.name: Silas Pike
anchors.role: carter on the stone road: takes stone from the works to Brackenford's market and brings berries back; robbed twice by the Coldwell outlaws; pays the gate-due and hates it
ties: pays the due to Wat Fenner
knows Marta Hale by sight and fears her people

anchors.name: Ruth Pike
anchors.role: cook for the works' kitchen; wants Silas off the road

anchors.name: Ezra Holt
anchors.role: quarryman who led the cutting on the ridge that broke into a giants' cairn; says he did not know

anchors.name: Dele Oyelaran
anchors.role: a Lanternquay builder who came after the Surge; lives on the poor terrace and works for low pay
ties: resented by Kettlebridge builders for undercutting them

settlements.name: Lanternquay
settlements.brief: The harbour town of concrete, neon and stalls, busy at all hours. Fishers, cooks and stall traders, builders who want to rebuild the lower quay, a few quay guards, a scribe, healers. The Harbour Warden speaks for the quay. They light tide lanterns for the drowned. They think Kettlebridge sells stone at a drowning man's price, and Brackenford is far and full of itself.
settlements.ledger: Lanternquay. The quay is for whoever works it. Lanterns for the drowned are lit at dusk; do not put them out.

anchors.name: Mara Quell
anchors.role: Harbour Warden; lost her brother in the Surge; wants stone for a seawall
ties: blames Josiah Crane for the price of stone
sends Juno Reyes up the fish road

anchors.name: Juno Reyes
anchors.role: runner on the fish road: carries cooked fish to Kettlebridge's market and stone back for the seawall
ties: childhood friend of Kai Ostrander, who deserted

anchors.name: Ilse Ostrander
anchors.role: keeps a noodle stall on the quay; her son Kai deserted the quay guard last year
ties: SECRET: Kai sent word he is alive at Coldwell; she has told no one

settlements.name: Highshelf
settlements.brief: The giants' settlement on its high shelf. Stone builders, masons, hunters, a few growers. Slow-spoken and patient; the elder decides after everyone has spoken. They keep cairns for their dead and never move one. Kettlebridge's quarrymen cut into a cairn last year and the elder closed the shelf to Kettlebridge. They are old friends of the small folk.
settlements.ledger: Highshelf. The cairns are not to be touched. The shelf does not trade with Kettlebridge.

anchors.name: Hollbrenna
anchors.role: elder of Highshelf; closed the shelf to Kettlebridge after the cairn cutting; her grandmother lies in that cairn

anchors.name: Orrum
anchors.role: Hollbrenna's son, stonecutter; expected to be elder after her
ties: wants Ezra Holt to answer for the cairn

anchors.name: Tavvik
anchors.role: a young hunter who carries meat down the giants' track to Kettlebridge and brings timber back up, against the elder's word
ties: Ezra Holt owes him for meat
SECRET: sweet on Prudence Vane of Kettlebridge, a cook who buys his meat

settlements.name: Fernhollow
settlements.brief: The small folk's hollow in the old forest. Gardeners and growers above all, cooks, carpenters who work fallen wood only, healers who make salves, a few fishers on the forest streams, traders and a pedlar who walks the east road, a keeper of the hollow's memory. Quick, curious, hospitable. They keep the Old Green. Old friends of the giants; wary of Kettlebridge's smoke; they avoid Brackenford's gate-due by trading south and east.
settlements.ledger: Fernhollow. Guests are fed before they are asked anything. No living tree of the old forest is felled.

anchors.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
anchors.role: Eldest of the hollow; keeps its memory and its gardens' calendar
ties: her mother and Hollbrenna were friends

anchors.name: Thistle Mossfoot
anchors.role: pedlar on the east road: carries fibre to Reedmoor's market and brings fish back
ties: friendly with the Coombes of the Lakemead

settlements.name: Thornby
settlements.brief: A fishing village on the north shore near Brackenford. Fishers, a few farmers and hunters, a cook. Owes Brackenford forty baskets of grain from the Lean Year and pays slowly in fish. Thinks old Edda at the north light wrecks boats.
settlements.ledger: Thornby. Nets are mended on the green. What the sea gives is shared with the widows first.

anchors.name: Osric Dunn
anchors.role: headman of Thornby; owes Brackenford's store forty baskets of grain and pays slowly in fish
ties: owes Aldric Marrow's town store forty baskets
thinks Edda at the north light wrecked his brother's boat

settlements.name: Elmwick
settlements.brief: A farming village in the southern woods. Farmers, hunters, a fisher, a cook, a builder. Claims the Lakemead as Elmwick's old common. One Lanternquay family from the Surge lives here.
settlements.ledger: Elmwick. The Lakemead was Elmwick's common before anyone let it.

anchors.name: Hob Garrow
anchors.role: elder of Elmwick; says Nell Sedge had no right to let the Lakemead
ties: quarrels with Nell Sedge over the Lakemead
grazed the Lakemead as a boy

settlements.name: Reedmoor
settlements.brief: A small village at the edge of the reeds on the south-east shore. Reed-cutters, fishers, a cook. Lets the Lakemead to the Coombes. Trades with Fernhollow's pedlar.
settlements.ledger: Reedmoor. The reeds are cut in turn. The Lakemead is let to the Coombes for grain.

anchors.name: Nell Sedge
anchors.role: headwoman of Reedmoor; let the Lakemead to the Coombes for grain

settlements.name: Coldwell
settlements.brief: The old Coldwell steading in the woods by the stone road between Brackenford and Kettlebridge. Its farmers lost their fields to Brackenford's store in the Lean Year and were outlawed when they would not leave their houses. They take a share from carriers on the stone road, by asking, threats or force. Joined by a deserter from Lanternquay and a runaway apprentice from Kettlebridge. They are people with reasons, not monsters.
settlements.ledger: Coldwell. These houses were built by Hales and Coldwells. The fields beyond the beck were ours.

anchors.name: Marta Hale
anchors.role: leads the Coldwell outlaws; a widow whose fields were taken; wants them back, or a pardon, or enough to live on
ties: hates the Tolleys who farm her fields

anchors.name: Robin Hale
anchors.role: Marta's son; had a fever last winter

anchors.name: Ned Hale
anchors.role: Marta's brother; was a farmer; does the threatening on the road
ties: brother of Marta Hale and Agnes Fenner

anchors.name: Kai Ostrander
anchors.role: a Lanternquay quay guard who deserted after the Surge; fights better than the others
ties: SECRET: sent word to his mother that he is alive

anchors.name: Pell
anchors.role: a runaway apprentice from Josiah Crane's foundry
ties: ran away from Josiah Crane before his indenture ended

settlements.name: Ashby
settlements.brief: Farms in the meadows near Brackenford. The Tolleys farm the old Coldwell fields for the Market Guild and fear the outlaws.
settlements.ledger: Ashby. Farmed for the Market Guild of Brackenford.

anchors.name: Hal Tolley
anchors.role: tenant of the Market Guild on the old Coldwell fields
ties: thinks the Hales had their chance

settlements.name: Highfold
settlements.brief: A herders' and hunters' fold in the hills between Kettlebridge and Highshelf. A human family who trade hides with the giants and are trusted on the shelf.

settlements.name: Sootwood
settlements.brief: Woodcutters and charcoal burners in the old forest above Lanternquay. They sell timber to the quay and think the seawall will never be built.

settlements.name: Lakemead
settlements.brief: The disputed meadow farm by the southern lake. The Coombes pay Reedmoor rent in grain; Elmwick says the meadow is Elmwick's common.

anchors.name: Jem Coombe
anchors.role: tenant of the Lakemead; pays Nell Sedge rent in grain; Elmwick folk have pulled down his fence twice

settlements.name: Saltings
settlements.brief: Salt pans and fish traps on the west shore below the hills: two households who keep to themselves.

settlements.name: the North Light
settlements.brief: A light on the north cape above Thornby, kept by an old woman and her grandson.
settlements.ledger: The light is lit every night.

anchors.name: Edda Wray
anchors.role: keeper of the north light; Thornby says she lit it wrong to wreck boats
ties: accused by Osric Dunn of wrecking his brother's boat
grandmother of the boy who lives with her

settlements.name: Tanglewood
settlements.brief: A healer's cottage in the old forest near Fernhollow: a woman who left Brackenford's chapel years ago, and those who come to her.

settlements.name: Ferncross
settlements.brief: Woodcutters at a crossing of tracks in the southern woods, selling timber to Elmwick and Reedmoor.
